If a claim is partly right, say exactly which part is wrong. Line numbers cited in the claims must be checked exactly (off-by-more-than-2 = IMPRECISE, wrong file = WRONG).

Read scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs, find the manifest/list of rule files, and report exactly which .claude/rules/*.md files are in it and which are omitted. Verify the five named omissions.

Verify those three exact line numbers and quote them. 7. "`.docs/architecture.md` misstates the stack: React Router v6 (actually 5.3.4 — the footer uses `useHistory`), Storybook 8 (actually 10.4.6), axe via `vitest-axe`/`axe-playwright` (neither installed), Playwright 'not yet configured' (7 projects, two workflows), 'all services mocked (MSW stubs)' (zero MSW references, and AGENTS.md bans mocking)." Both contradict CODEOWNERS on PDP ownership — CODEOWNERS says Squad B." — For .claude/rules/squadA.md and squadB.md: extract every repo path each claims as territory, count them, and test each for existence on disk. Report the real counts (e.g. "squadA lists N paths, M exist"). Check `git log -1 --format=%ad` for each file in .claude/rules/ to test the "six weeks older" claim. Check what squadA.md/squadB.md say about overrides/app/pages/product-detail/ and compare with CODEOWNERS line 162.
10. "`sprintScope.md` is two months stale. Last commit 2026-06-25. It says 'Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress)' while its own table puts today (2026-08-25) in Sprint 5. Six skills cite it." Verify: `git log -1 --format=%ad -- .docs/memory/sprintScope.md`, the "Sprint 0" text, the sprint table dates, and count how many files under .claude/skills/ reference sprintScope.
11. "`projectState.md` ... still lists SFCC-55 as 'In Progress: PR #59'". Verify in .docs/memory/projectState.md.
12. "AGENTS.md:37 names the dead path `tests/lighthouserc.js`." Verify AGENTS.md line 37 exactly.
13. "The SOW allows 10 defects, no Sev3" — grep .docs/ for any SOW/defect-budget statement and report whether this is supported by any repo doc (or UNVERIFIABLE).
14. "Confluence 04.71 (page 400195600)" story decomposition "Encoded nowhere in this repo — nothing in `.claude/`, `.docs/` or CI mentions or enforces it." Grep the repo for `400195600` and for `04.71` / "Level 1" component epic language.
15. "Of 18 documented integrations: 2 live, 5 partially wired, 11 doc-only." Count the files in .docs/integration/ (pattern NN-*.md) and report the actual number of documented integrations. Note 2+5+11=18 — check the arithmetic against the actual doc count.

     3	description: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
     4	---
     5	
     6	Scaffold a new Zimmermann custom component.
     7	
     8	The component name is: $ARGUMENTS
     9	
    10	## Conventions
    11	
    12	Follow [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) (naming, folder layout,
    13	cross-cutting rules), [components.md](../../rules/components.md) (props types, JSDoc policy,
    14	composition, Storybook categorisation), and [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra token usage)
    15	— together the single source of truth for scaffolding. Higher-level project rules live in
    16	[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do not restate rules here — read those files before
    17	scaffolding.
    18	
    19	Key implications for scaffolding:
    20	- Component lives in its own folder: `componentName/index.tsx` (Zimmermann-authored) or
    21	  `component-name/index.tsx` (override of a base SF component).
    22	- Props type named `<ComponentName>Props`, declared at the top of `index.tsx` by default.
    23	- Storybook story is mandatory; Vitest only when the component owns non-trivial logic.
    24	
    25	## Steps
    26	
    27	1. Read one nearby existing custom component under [overrides/app/components/](../../../overrides/app/components/) to match code style, import order, and Chakra usage. If no Zimmermann-authored component exists yet, read a base template component from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and convert the style to TypeScript + Chakra props.
    28	
    29	2. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`:
    30	   - Functional React component, named export (`export function <ComponentName>`) plus default export.
    31	   - `type <ComponentName>Props = { ... }` at the top of the file.
    32	   - JSDoc above the component if it will be consumed by ≥2 callers (shared/Tier 2).
    33	   - Chakra primitives for layout (`Box`, `Flex`, `Text`, etc.) using theme tokens — no hardcoded hex, pixel spacing, or raw font sizes.
    34	   - No data-fetching hooks of any kind (commerce SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or React Query) — accept data as props; the parent (a page or container component) owns data fetching. See components.md → Composition → Container/presentational separation. Exception: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called directly — they read from a Provider mounted once at the app root and degrade gracefully with none present, so they don't create the reuse problem this rule exists to prevent. See components.md's exception note for the full reasoning.
    35	
    36	3. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.stories.tsx` — but first decide
    37	   if a story is needed at all. Per [components.md](../../rules/components.md) →
    38	   **Storybook**, purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent
    39	   don't need their own story; cover their variants via the parent. If a story *is* needed:
    40	   - Storybook 8.6 CSF3 default export.
    41	   - Pick the right category prefix from components.md — `Foundation/`, `Elements/`,
    42	     `Layout/`, `Commerce/`, `Forms/`, `Pages/`, or `Contentful/`. Ask the developer if it's
    43	     not obvious which one fits (with your recommendation).
    44	   - `title: '<Category>/<ComponentName>'` (e.g. `'Commerce/ProductTile'`,
    45	     `'Layout/Header'`).
    46	   - At least one named export `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states only —
    47	     not every prop combination.
    48	   - Add a `play` function only if the component has interactive behaviour worth asserting.
    49	
    50	4. If the component owns non-trivial logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping decisions, event wiring), create `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx` (Vitest) in the same folder — even if that logic's effects are also covered by a hook's own test or a parent's assembly-level Storybook `play`. Resolve any duplication by mocking the hook/child whose internals are proven elsewhere and testing only this component's own contract, not by skipping the file. See testing.md's note under "What to test (and what to skip)". Skip only when the component has no branching/decision logic at all (pure prop interpolation).
    51	
    52	5. Optional: if the props type exceeds ~30 lines or will be consumed by sibling files, move it to `types.ts` in the same folder. Otherwise leave it inline.
    53	
    54	6. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm zero new errors.
    55	
    56	## Constraints
    57	
    58	- Do not modify any existing files (no auto-wiring into routes, parents, or the theme registry).
    59	- Do not add npm packages — see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 7.
    60	- Do not import from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` source directly — re-export from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` paths.

=== integration/index.md ===
# PWA Integration Design Documents

These documents describe each external system that the Zimmermann PWA storefront interacts with **from the PWA layer** — either browser-direct or proxied through the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer. Each system has its own document covering purpose, scope, browser-side architecture, authentication, data exchange, consent gating, performance, multi-region behaviour, graceful degradation, security and privacy, and the open items requiring client input before implementation.

> **Scope.** PWA-layer only (browser-direct and MRT-proxied). Backend integrations consumed by SFCC via MuleSoft (NewStore writes, AP21 — including the inbound product + pricing feed, Omneo profile sync, Emarsys, Narvar back office, Avalara, GiveX validate / redeem / refund, Transperfect) are addressed by the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft middleware design and are not duplicated here.

The documents are grouped by role rather than by runtime load order. A reader new to the system can start at the top and build a mental model from the most central systems outwards.

### Commerce backbone

The data sources every storefront page depends on.

| #   | System                                | Purpose                                                                | Document                             |
| --- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| 1   | **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI)** | All commerce data — catalogue, basket, customer, orders.               | [01-sfcc.md](01-sfcc.md)             |
| 2   | **Contentful**                        | CMS — Delivery API, Preview API, Studio live preview, publish webhook. | [02-contentful.md](02-contentful.md) |

### Account and customer data

Server-mediated reads that bypass SFCC for data the storefront fetches on behalf of the customer.

| #   | System                          | Purpose                                                                                        | Document                         |
| --- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 3   | **MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads)** | Order history, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock via MRT proxy.                  | [03-mulesoft.md](03-mulesoft.md) |
| 4   | **Omneo**                       | Communication Preferences iFrame in My Account.                                                | [04-omneo.md](04-omneo.md)       |
| 5   | **GiveX (balance check)**       | My Account gift card balance check via MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX.                                 | [05-givex.md](05-givex.md)       |
| 6   | **Booxi**                       | My Account boutique appointment history via MRT proxy (PWA → MRT → Booxi). Scope/timeline TBC. | [06-booxi.md](06-booxi.md)       |

### Checkout cluster

The buying flow.

| #   | System                            | Purpose                                                                                          | Document                               |
| --- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| 7   | **Adyen**                         | Browser-side payment Drop-in for SFCC-owned domestic checkout.                                   | [07-adyen.md](07-adyen.md)             |
| 8   | **Global-e**                      | International checkout (HK, ME, EU international, US international).                             | [08-global-e.md](08-global-e.md)       |
| 9   | **Google Maps Platform (Places)** | Address autocomplete at checkout, MRT-proxied.                                                   | [09-google-maps.md](09-google-maps.md) |
| 10  | **Google reCAPTCHA**              | Bot protection on register / login forms — browser loads script, MRT verifies token server-side. | [10-recaptcha.md](10-recaptcha.md)     |
| 11  | **Narvar**                        | Estimated Delivery Date widget at checkout, domestic only.                                       | [11-narvar.md](11-narvar.md)           |

### Cross-cutting overlays

Consent, analytics, and customer service — applied across every page rather than tied to a specific journey.

| #   | System                 | Purpose                                                                                          | Document                               |
| --- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| 12  | **Didomi**             | Consent Management Platform — gatekeeper for every browser-loaded third-party script.            | [12-didomi.md](12-didomi.md)           |
| 13  | **Google Tag Manager** | Data layer, Consent Mode v2, downstream tag orchestration via Tell No Lies.                      | [13-gtm.md](13-gtm.md)                 |
| 14  | **Inside Chat**        | Customer-service chat widget.                                                                    | [14-inside-chat.md](14-inside-chat.md) |
| 15  | **Optimizely Web**     | A/B testing and personalisation — frontend-direct script (not in GTM).                           | [15-optimizely.md](15-optimizely.md)   |
| 16  | **Crazy Egg**          | Heatmaps and session recording — frontend-direct script (not in GTM).                            | [16-crazyegg.md](16-crazyegg.md)       |
| 17  | **Measmerize**         | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP.                                                 | [17-measmerize.md](17-measmerize.md)   |
| 18  | **Vimeo**              | Product video (PDP gallery) and editorial video (homepage and content pages via Contentful CMS). | [18-vimeo.md](18-vimeo.md)             |

## Note on runtime load order

The ordering above is **for reading**, not for runtime. At runtime, **Didomi loads first** (document 11) because every other browser-loaded third-party script — GTM, Inside Chat, the Narvar widget, the Google Maps proxy call, and the Adyen Drop-in — is gated by Didomi consent. Each integration document records its own consent posture; the Didomi document is the single contract that all the others honour.

## Cross-cutting principles

All 15 claims verified. Report below.

---

## 1. `overrides.md` missing, referenced 3× — **TRUE** (with a history caveat)

- `.claude/rules/` contains 11 files; `overrides.md` is **not** among them (`git ls-files .claude/rules/` and `ls`), and `git cat-file -e` confirms it is absent from `HEAD`, `develop`, and `origin/develop`.
- Exactly three references, at the exact lines claimed:
  - `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:4` — `Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a`
  - `:112` — `base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override`
  - `:179` — `matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put`

**Caveat the doc should carry:** the file is not fictional. It exists on two live branches — added by commit `a6842cf` (2026-08-14, Han Lee, `feat(rules): add overrides.md pre-flight rules for SFCC override components`), reachable from `feature/f2r-component-registry` and `feature/pdp-token-class-spike`. This is an unmerged-branch dangling link, not an invented reference.

## 2. `overrideStyling.md` orphaned from AGENTS.md — **TRUE on the literal test, IMPRECISE as characterised**

- `grep -c "overrideStyling" AGENTS.md` → **0**. Confirmed. `CLAUDE.md` is a one-line `@AGENTS.md` stub, so 0 there too.
- AGENTS.md:121-124 enumerates the auto-loading rules by name and omits it: `*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically: [conventions.md]... [typescript.md]... [css.md]... and [components.md]...*`
- **"Orphaned" overstates it.** It is auto-loaded by Claude Code regardless (it is present verbatim in this session's project-instruction block), and it is inbound-linked from `.claude/rules/css.md:22,30,38`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md:60`, `CODEOWNERS:179`, `.docs/architecture.md:136`, and seven source files (e.g. `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:14`, `footer/footer.css.ts:8`, `theme/components/footerShared.ts:6,16`). It is un-indexed by AGENTS.md, not unreferenced.

## 3. syncCursorRules.mjs manifest omissions — **TRUE**

`scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs` `MANIFEST` (lines 61-210) references exactly **6** `.claude/rules/` files:

| In manifest | Line |
|---|---|
| `frozenFiles.md` | 64 |
| `protectedFiles.md` | 75 |
| `conventions.md` | 86 |
| `squadA.md` | 97 |
| `squadB.md` | 108 |
| `testing.md` | 119 |

**Omitted (all five named, confirmed):** `overrideStyling.md`, `css.md`, `components.md`, `typescript.md`, `tagging.md`.

Additional finding not in the claim: the `compile` entry for `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (lines 159-173) drops `testing.md` too, so Copilot gets 5 of the 11 rules files.

## 4. Zero atomic-design terms in `components.md` / `conventions.md` — **TRUE**

Occurrence counts (case-insensitive, `grep -oi | wc -l`):

| Term | components.md | conventions.md |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-kits` | 0 | 0 |
| `atoms` | 0 | 0 |
| `molecules` | 0 | 0 |
| `organisms` | 0 | 0 |

Sharpens the claim: `.claude/rules/testing.md:81` *does* use the path (`vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', ...)`), so the gap is specific to the two authoring-convention files — which is the worse of the two places for it to be missing.

## 5. `new-component/SKILL.md:29` scaffolds flat — **TRUE**

`.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md:29`:
> `2. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`:`

Corroborated by line 20: `` - Component lives in its own folder: `componentName/index.tsx` (Zimmermann-authored) or `component-name/index.tsx` (override of a base SF component). `` No `ui-kits/` anywhere in the file.

## 6. `architecture.md` self-contradiction on component paths — **TRUE**

- `:136` — `...beside its component as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g. `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` — governed by that component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead).`
- `:130` — `- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.`
- `:139` — `- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/``

All three line numbers exact. `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- '**/components/custom/*'` returns **nothing**; `find overrides -type d -name custom` returns nothing; the only two occurrences of the string `components/custom` in the entire repo are architecture.md:130 and :139. Directory has never existed on any branch.

## 7. Stack misstatements — **TRUE on all five, with one sub-claim WRONG**

| Sub-claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| React Router v6 | **TRUE** | `architecture.md:66` — `\| Routing \| React Router v6 \|`. | axe via `vitest-axe`/`axe-playwright` | **TRUE** | `architecture.md:80` — `\| Accessibility testing \| axe-core (via `vitest-axe` / `axe-playwright`) \|`. Neither installed (`node_modules/vitest-axe`, `node_modules/axe-playwright`, `node_modules/jest-axe` all absent). `axe-core` itself **is** present, transitively. |
| Playwright "not yet configured" | **TRUE** | `architecture.md:81` — `\| E2E tests (planned) \| Playwright \| Not yet configured \|`. `playwright.config.js` defines **7** projects: `p0`, `chromium`, `mobile-chrome`, `a11y-mobile`, `a11y-desktop`, `extra-features-desktop`, `extra-features-mobile` (lines 53-85), driven by `.github/workflows/qa.yml` and `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml`. Same doc contradicts itself at `:104`/`:106`. |
| "zero MSW references, and AGENTS.md bans mocking" | **WRONG** | The architecture.md quote is right (`:95` — `\| 1 \| **Local** \| Digital \| ... \| All services mocked (MSW stubs) \| `npm start` \|`), but the parenthetical is false on both halves. **14** MSW references exist outside `node_modules`/`package-lock.json`, and `msw@1.3.5` **is installed**. AGENTS.md does not ban mocking outright — `AGENTS.md:128`: "No MSW or hardcoded fixtures **in production paths**", and `:153` explicitly says "(The no-MSW rule in Rules applies to production paths only.)" `.claude/rules/testing.md:73` **permits** it: "**MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests". The real defect at `:95` is different and narrower: MSW is a *test* tool being described as the runtime data source for local dev. |

## 8. `testing.md` line numbers — **IMPRECISE** (both off by exactly 28; substance correct)

- `@storybook/test` is at **`:115`**, not `:87`. Line 87 is `### Commerce SDK hooks`.
- "never reach into `document`" is at **`:128`**, not `:100`. Line 100 is blank.
- Both statements do exist and say what is claimed: `:115` `import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'`; `:128` `- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.`
- The portal point stands: `grep -i portal .claude/rules/testing.md` → **zero hits**. No carve-out anywhere in the file.

The uniform +28 offset means the doc was written against a `testing.md` predating the `ZimmIcon`/Vitest-gap block (lines ~76-85). Re-cite before publishing.

## 9. Squad rules — **MIXED: two sub-claims WRONG, two TRUE**

**Path counts — WRONG on squadA, TRUE on squadB.**

squadA.md's territory block (lines 33-53) lists **21** paths, not 18 — and **4 exist**:

| Exists | Missing (17) |
|---|---|
| `overrides/app/pages/home/`, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, `overrides/app/components/header/`, `overrides/app/components/footer/` | `pages/product-list/`, `pages/product-list/partials/`, `pages/cart/`, `pages/checkout/`, `pages/checkout/partials/`, `pages/checkout-one-click/`, `pages/confirmation/`, `components/drawer-menu/`, `components/list-menu/`, `components/sf-payments-express/`, `components/sf-payments-express-buttons/`, `components/multiship/`, `components/bonus-product-view-modal/`, `hooks/use-checkout-auto-select.ts`, `hooks/use-multiship.ts`, `hooks/use-pickup-shipment.ts`, `hooks/use-sf-payments.ts` |

18 is not recoverable by any reading: the YAML frontmatter `paths:` block (lines 3-21) has **19** entries; deduping the two `partials/` sub-paths from the territory block gives **19**. The "4 exist" half is correct. **Use "21 listed, 4 exist".**

squadB.md's territory block (lines 23-31) lists **9** paths, **0** exist. **TRUE, exactly as claimed.**

**"Six weeks older than every other rules file" — WRONG.** `git log -1 --format=%ad`:

| File | Date | | File | Date |

| `conventions.md` | **2026-07-10** | | `overrideStyling.md` | 2026-08-24 |
| `typescript.md` | **2026-07-10** | | `protectedFiles.md` | 2026-08-24 |

`conventions.md` and `typescript.md` are four days **older**. The squad files are ~5.9 weeks older than the *newest* files, so "roughly six weeks behind the actively-maintained rules" is defensible; "older than every other rules file" is not.

**PDP ownership contradiction — TRUE, and worse than stated (it is a three-way conflict).**
- `CODEOWNERS:162` — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/                           @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` (under `# ── TIER 3: Squad B ownership ──`, line 160). Only occurrence of `product-detail` in CODEOWNERS.

- `squadB.md:41` — `- `product-detail/` and `product-list/` are Squad A territory — do not modify without Squad A Lead approval.`
- And `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs:35` puts `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**` in `SQUAD_B_GLOBS` — so the sync script agrees with CODEOWNERS and disagrees with the rule file it is generating from. Worth adding; it means the Cursor rule shipped to developers has Squad B globs attached to Squad A's territory text.

## 10. `sprintScope.md` stale — **TRUE on all four sub-claims**

- `git log -1 --date=iso -- .docs/memory/sprintScope.md` → `2026-06-25 14:15:27 +1000 | decc0c3 | docs: Updated squad split + github PR template`. Two months to the day.

- `:77` — `## Sprint 5 — 24 Aug – 4 Sep` — today (2026-08-25) falls inside it.
- Exactly **6** files under `.claude/skills/` reference it: `session-start`, `generate-changelog`, `code-quality`, `qa-generate`, `feature-spec`, `onboarding`.

Strengthener available: it is also load-bearing in `AGENTS.md:43` (Hard Rule 14, "Never reference code from a later sprint"), `.claude/rules/conventions.md:117`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:10`, and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md:27`. > `8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).`

`tests/lighthouserc.js` does not exist; the real file is `./lighthouserc.js` (repo root, 800 bytes). `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/testing.md` both correctly say `lighthouserc.js` — AGENTS.md is the sole outlier, and it is the Tier 1 governance file.

- `grep -rniE "level 1 .*epic|level 2 .*epic|component epic|page epic"` → **0 hits**

`.docs/integration/` contains exactly **18** files matching `NN-*.md` (01-sfcc through 18-vimeo) plus `index.md`. The arithmetic 2+5+11=18 is internally consistent and matches the doc count.
